findings.text: [C] puts the stars, the crescent and the soft hills in one small picture, the cosmic and the cozy side by side, but its tiny "4" is gone at the smallest tinted size and its home-screen name is cut to "Paint by Mo...", so under the icon it never finishes saying what it is.
[D]'s crescent cradling a "3" stays clear at all three tinted sizes and in the dimmed bedtime view, and "Moonlight" fits under it whole: calm, no fuss, a picture any child can read.
[A]'s blotchy full moon looks more like a stained cookie than a moon at small sizes, and at night its dark purple spots make the face look bruised rather than gentle.
[B]'s big "6" on a hill says numbers plainly, but nothing in it says night or wonder, and "Paint by Heart" reads warmly yet tells you less than the picture does.
None of the four carries anything a family would hesitate to hand a child; they are all kind and quiet, which is the right temperature for a bedtime app.
